title: Local demographic history does not reduce to static island architecture in Antarctic penguins

already_established: Black-legged kittiwake breeder redistribution and breeding-habitat selection can track previous local reproductive success.
Experimental manipulation in kittiwakes shows neighbouring reproductive performance can affect attendance, site fidelity and recruitment.
A 2024 Adelie penguin study reported a strong one-year-lagged breeding-success-growth association interpreted as coherent with public-information use.
Palmer snow, terrain and geomorphology influence subcolony persistence.
Ross Island mark-recapture work documents age- and colony-dependent pre-breeder movement and recruitment.
not_novel_here: the hypothesis that colonial seabirds can use conspecific performance as public information
the existence of landscape effects on Adelie breeding sites
the existence of pre-breeder movement among Ross Island colonies
target_novelty: denominator-separated lag-2 evidence that a specific late-season colony-wide state carries short-lived information about subsequent within-island redistribution after shared annual forcing, prior size and persistent colony identity are controlled
a lag profile that rejects a predeclared 4-5-year recruitment-echo pattern
failure of an independent nest-level reproductive metric to reproduce the colony-wide-state association, showing metric-specific biological information rather than generic reproductive success
the cross-scale contrast between locally informative dynamic history and non-confirmatory, spatial-support-sensitive transfer through static Antarctic island descriptors

writing_rules: Explicitly acknowledge that public-information and performance-based habitat-selection hypotheses predate this study.
Explicitly acknowledge the 2024 Adelie one-year lag result before claiming novelty.
Describe lag 1 as non-novel and mechanically coupled in this analysis.
State that the novel Palmer inference is the denominator-separated temporal signature plus metric-specific non-replication, not proof of public-information use.
Published Ross literature may be cited as motivation, but no unpublished Ross behavioral result may enter Results, Abstract conclusions or evidence claims.
Keep the Part II non-confirmatory result inferentially independent.
prohibited_language: first evidence that Adelie penguins use public information
